lesson.title: Multiplying a 2-Digit Number by a 2-Digit Number
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: So far you've multiplied a bigger number by a single digit. Today, both numbers get bigger — but the area model still works, just with more pieces to add.

Let's multiply 23 x 14. Break BOTH numbers into place value: 23 = 20 + 3, and 14 = 10 + 4. Now you need four partial products, one for each pair: 20 x 10 = 200, 20 x 4 = 80, 3 x 10 = 30, and 3 x 4 = 12. Add all four together: 200 + 80 + 30 + 12 = 322. It helps to draw a rectangle split into a 2x2 grid, with 23's pieces along the top and 14's pieces along the side — each of the four inner boxes is one partial product.

Try it yourself with 32 x 15: break both numbers apart, find all four partial products, then add them together. Two-digit by two-digit multiplication is really just four smaller multiplications and one addition.

objectives: Multiply a 2-digit number by a 2-digit number using the area model (4 partial products)
Draw a 2x2 area-model grid to organize the four partial products
materialsNeeded: Optional: grid paper for drawing the area model
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the single-digit-multiplier area model from Days 1-2.
2. Work through 23 x 14 together, drawing the 2x2 grid and labeling all four partial products.
3. Have the child try 32 x 15 independently, drawing their own grid.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: real-world word problems using this skill.
differentiationTips: Struggling: pre-draw the 2x2 grid and have the child fill in only the four partial products and the final sum
Ready for more: try a 3-digit x 2-digit problem to see how many partial products that would need (six)
Drawing the grid is genuinely helpful here, not just decorative — encourage it even for children who are quick with the arithmetic itself
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 4 4.NBT.5 (multiplying two two-digit numbers), extending the area-model approach from Days 1-2 to a genuinely new case — four partial products instead of two or three.

generationData.instructions: Use the area model (four partial products) to solve each problem.
